lessons.title: Useful intermediate vocabulary
lessons.pattern: 자기/자신, 훨씬, 관련하다, 주위, 일단, 전혀/별로
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 34 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.prompt: 그는 ___ 아버지에 대해 신경(을) 안 써
cards.translation: He doesn’t care about his father
cards.explanation: This is an HTSK vocabulary lesson covering 자기/자신, 훨씬, 관련하다, 주위, 일단, 전혀/별로, weight expressions and ~거리다 words. In this sentence, “자기” completes the blank in “그는 자기 아버지에 대해 신경(을) 안 써” and gives it the meaning “He doesn’t care about his father”. There is no single attachment rule. Learn each vocabulary item with its normal particles and endings; ~거리다 is part of the word-building material in the lesson.

Learn each vocabulary item with its normal particles and endings; ~거리다 is part of the word-building material in the lesson.

lessons.title: Expressing possibility with ~ㄹ/을 것 같다
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 35 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.translation: I will probably eat rice/I might eat rice
cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을 것 같다 expresses a guess, possibility or impression: it seems or might be. HTSK also shows the common expression 그럴 것 같다. In this sentence, “것 같다” completes the blank in “나는 밥을 먹을 것 같다” and gives it the meaning “I will probably eat rice/I might eat rice”. Attach ~ㄹ 것 같다 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을 것 같다 after another consonant. Use the past and present modifier forms for other time references.

cards.translation: I will probably go fishing with my friends tomorrow
cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을 것 같다 expresses a guess, possibility or impression: it seems or might be. HTSK also shows the common expression 그럴 것 같다. In this sentence, “것 같아” completes the blank in “저는 친구들이랑 내일 낚시를 할 것 같아요” and gives it the meaning “I will probably go fishing with my friends tomorrow”. Attach ~ㄹ 것 같다 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을 것 같다 after another consonant. Use the past and present modifier forms for other time references.

cards.translation: Dad will probably not like that
cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을 것 같다 expresses a guess, possibility or impression: it seems or might be. HTSK also shows the common expression 그럴 것 같다. In this sentence, “것 같아” completes the blank in “우리 아빠는 저것을 싫어할 것 같아” and gives it the meaning “Dad will probably not like that”. Attach ~ㄹ 것 같다 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을 것 같다 after another consonant. Use the past and present modifier forms for other time references.

cards.translation: The teacher probably won’t do (teach) that lesson
cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을 것 같다 expresses a guess, possibility or impression: it seems or might be. HTSK also shows the common expression 그럴 것 같다. In this sentence, “것 같아” completes the blank in “선생님이 그 수업을 하지 않을 것 같아요” and gives it the meaning “The teacher probably won’t do (teach) that lesson”. Attach ~ㄹ 것 같다 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을 것 같다 after another consonant. Use the past and present modifier forms for other time references.

cards.translation: My boyfriend probably won’t respond
cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을 것 같다 expresses a guess, possibility or impression: it seems or might be. HTSK also shows the common expression 그럴 것 같다. In this sentence, “것 같아” completes the blank in “남자 친구가 답장하지 않을 것 같아요” and gives it the meaning “My boyfriend probably won’t respond”. Attach ~ㄹ 것 같다 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을 것 같다 after another consonant. Use the past and present modifier forms for other time references.

lessons.meaning: ~ㄹ/을 것 같다 expresses a guess, possibility or impression: it seems or might be. HTSK also shows the common expression 그럴 것 같다.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when making a prediction or describing an impression without presenting it as a firm fact.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~ㄹ 것 같다 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을 것 같다 after another consonant. Use the past and present modifier forms for other time references.

Probably / I think so / It seems so

lessons.title: Saying something looks/seems like ~같이 보이다 and ~아/어 보이다
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 36 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.translation: You look like a monkey
cards.explanation: ~같이 보이다 means to look or seem like a noun, and ~아/어 보이다 means to look a certain way. HTSK also applies the idea to smell and taste. In this sentence, “같이 보여” completes the blank in “너는 원숭이 같이 보여” and gives it the meaning “You look like a monkey”. Use noun + 같이 보이다, or attach ~아/어 보이다 to an adjective stem using the normal 아/어 rule.

cards.translation: My boyfriend looks like the professor
cards.explanation: ~같이 보이다 means to look or seem like a noun, and ~아/어 보이다 means to look a certain way. HTSK also applies the idea to smell and taste. In this sentence, “같이 보여요” completes the blank in “저의 남자친구는 교수님 같이 보여요” and gives it the meaning “My boyfriend looks like the professor”. Use noun + 같이 보이다, or attach ~아/어 보이다 to an adjective stem using the normal 아/어 rule.

cards.translation: You look like a high school student
cards.explanation: ~같이 보이다 means to look or seem like a noun, and ~아/어 보이다 means to look a certain way. HTSK also applies the idea to smell and taste. In this sentence, “같이 보여” completes the blank in “너는 고등학생 같이 보여” and gives it the meaning “You look like a high school student”. Use noun + 같이 보이다, or attach ~아/어 보이다 to an adjective stem using the normal 아/어 rule.

cards.translation: My girlfriend looks like a celebrity
cards.explanation: ~같이 보이다 means to look or seem like a noun, and ~아/어 보이다 means to look a certain way. HTSK also applies the idea to smell and taste. In this sentence, “같이 보여요” completes the blank in “저의 여자친구는 연예인 같이 보여요” and gives it the meaning “My girlfriend looks like a celebrity”. Use noun + 같이 보이다, or attach ~아/어 보이다 to an adjective stem using the normal 아/어 rule.

cards.translation: I look smarter than that person
cards.explanation: ~같이 보이다 means to look or seem like a noun, and ~아/어 보이다 means to look a certain way. HTSK also applies the idea to smell and taste. In this sentence, “보여요” completes the blank in “저는 그 사람보다 더 똑똑해 보여요” and gives it the meaning “I look smarter than that person”. Use noun + 같이 보이다, or attach ~아/어 보이다 to an adjective stem using the normal 아/어 rule.

lessons.source_title: Saying something looks/seems like ~같이 보이다 and ~아/어 보이다
lessons.meaning: ~같이 보이다 means to look or seem like a noun, and ~아/어 보이다 means to look a certain way. HTSK also applies the idea to smell and taste.
lessons.when_to_use: Use these forms for an impression based on appearance, smell, taste or a visible condition.
lessons.how_to_build: Use noun + 같이 보이다, or attach ~아/어 보이다 to an adjective stem using the normal 아/어 rule.
examples: 왜 그렇게 행복해 보여요?
Why do you look so happy?
저의 여자친구는 어제 너무 슬퍼 보였어요

그 남자 종아리가 아주 강해 보여요
That man’s calf looks very strong
이 원룸은 깨끗해 보여요
This (studio) apartment looks clean

lessons.title: Giving a reason with ~아/어서
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 37 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.translation: It is Sunday, so I want to go to the park
cards.explanation: ~아/어서 connects clauses with a natural cause-and-result relationship: because or so. In this sentence, “일요일이어서” completes the blank in “일요일이어서 공원에 가고 싶어요” and gives it the meaning “It is Sunday, so I want to go to the park”. Attach ~아서 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem, ~어서 after other vowels, and ~해서 after 하다. The second clause normally carries the tense.

cards.translation: It is Sunday, so I want to go to the park
cards.explanation: ~아/어서 connects clauses with a natural cause-and-result relationship: because or so. In this sentence, “일요일이라서” completes the blank in “일요일이라서 공원에 가고 싶어요” and gives it the meaning “It is Sunday, so I want to go to the park”. Attach ~아서 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem, ~어서 after other vowels, and ~해서 after 하다. The second clause normally carries the tense.

cards.translation: She is a pretty girl, so she is probably not smart
cards.explanation: ~아/어서 connects clauses with a natural cause-and-result relationship: because or so. In this sentence, “여자여서” completes the blank in “예쁜 여자여서 똑똑하지 않을 것 같아” and gives it the meaning “She is a pretty girl, so she is probably not smart”. Attach ~아서 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem, ~어서 after other vowels, and ~해서 after 하다. The second clause normally carries the tense.

cards.translation: She is a pretty girl, so she is probably not smart
cards.explanation: ~아/어서 connects clauses with a natural cause-and-result relationship: because or so. In this sentence, “여자라서” completes the blank in “예쁜 여자라서 똑똑하지 않을 것 같아” and gives it the meaning “She is a pretty girl, so she is probably not smart”. Attach ~아서 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem, ~어서 after other vowels, and ~해서 after 하다. The second clause normally carries the tense.

cards.prompt: 이번 주말이 ___ 우리 엄마 집에 갈 거예요
cards.translation: This weekend is a long weekend, so I will go to our mom’s house
cards.explanation: ~아/어서 connects clauses with a natural cause-and-result relationship: because or so. In this sentence, “연휴라서” completes the blank in “이번 주말이 연휴라서 우리 엄마 집에 갈 거예요” and gives it the meaning “This weekend is a long weekend, so I will go to our mom’s house”. Attach ~아서 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem, ~어서 after other vowels, and ~해서 after 하다. The second clause normally carries the tense.

lessons.meaning: ~아/어서 connects clauses with a natural cause-and-result relationship: because or so.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when the first clause naturally explains the result in the second clause, especially in everyday speech.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~아서 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem, ~어서 after other vowels, and ~해서 after 하다. The second clause normally carries the tense.
examples: 저는 배고파서 밥을 먹고 싶어요
I am hungry, therefore I want to eat
나중에 밥이 없을 거라서 저는 지금 먹고 싶어요

lessons.title: Giving a reason with ~기 때문에
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 38 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.translation: I don’t want to die because I am happy
cards.explanation: ~기 때문에 gives a clear reason meaning because or due to and works across past, present and future contexts. In this sentence, “행복하기 때문에” completes the blank in “저는 행복하기 때문에 죽고 싶지 않아요” and gives it the meaning “I don’t want to die because I am happy”. Nominalize the verb or adjective with ~기 and add 때문에; a noun can be followed directly by 때문에.

cards.translation: I don’t know how much this shirt costs because there is no price tag
cards.explanation: ~기 때문에 gives a clear reason meaning because or due to and works across past, present and future contexts. In this sentence, “없기 때문에” completes the blank in “이 셔츠에 가격표가 없기 때문에 얼마인지 몰라요” and gives it the meaning “I don’t know how much this shirt costs because there is no price tag”. Nominalize the verb or adjective with ~기 and add 때문에; a noun can be followed directly by 때문에.

cards.prompt: 학생들이 교복을 ___ 다 똑같은 옷을 입었어요
cards.translation: All the students wore exactly the same clothes because they wear uniforms
cards.explanation: ~기 때문에 gives a clear reason meaning because or due to and works across past, present and future contexts. In this sentence, “입기 때문에” completes the blank in “학생들이 교복을 입기 때문에 다 똑같은 옷을 입었어요” and gives it the meaning “All the students wore exactly the same clothes because they wear uniforms”. Nominalize the verb or adjective with ~기 and add 때문에; a noun can be followed directly by 때문에.

cards.translation: I like those kinds of movies because I am a man
cards.explanation: ~기 때문에 gives a clear reason meaning because or due to and works across past, present and future contexts. In this sentence, “남자이기 때문에” completes the blank in “내가 남자이기 때문에 그런 영화를 좋아해” and gives it the meaning “I like those kinds of movies because I am a man”. Nominalize the verb or adjective with ~기 and add 때문에; a noun can be followed directly by 때문에.

cards.translation: I’m going to go to another place because the entrance is too far
cards.explanation: ~기 때문에 gives a clear reason meaning because or due to and works across past, present and future contexts. In this sentence, “멀기 때문에” completes the blank in “입구가 멀기 때문에 다른 곳으로 갈 거예요” and gives it the meaning “I’m going to go to another place because the entrance is too far”. Nominalize the verb or adjective with ~기 and add 때문에; a noun can be followed directly by 때문에.

lessons.meaning: ~기 때문에 gives a clear reason meaning because or due to and works across past, present and future contexts.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when explaining a reason clearly, especially when the reason deserves emphasis or appears in writing.
lessons.how_to_build: Nominalize the verb or adjective with ~기 and add 때문에; a noun can be followed directly by 때문에.
examples: 저는 배고프기 때문에 밥을 먹고 싶어요
I want to eat because I am hungry
지금 공부를 하고 있기 때문에 너랑 통화하고 싶지 않아
I don’t want to talk with you on the phone because I’m studying now
투자자가 없기 때문에 우리는 다른 방법으로 할 거예요
We will do it another way because there are no investors
무릎이 아프기 때문에 저는 걸어가기 싫어요

lessons.title: Honorific ~시~
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 39 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.translation: Now, the principal will speak for a moment
cards.explanation: The honorific ~시~ marks respect toward the person performing an action. HTSK also introduces special honorific vocabulary. In this sentence, “하시” completes the blank in “지금 교장선생님께서 잠깐 말씀을 하시겠습니다” and gives it the meaning “Now, the principal will speak for a moment”. Insert ~시~ into the conjugated verb or adjective before the speech ending: 가시다, 읽으시다, and polite ~세요 forms.

cards.translation: Did you listen (well/carefully) to what your teacher said?
cards.explanation: The honorific ~시~ marks respect toward the person performing an action. HTSK also introduces special honorific vocabulary. In this sentence, “하시” completes the blank in “선생님이 하시는 말씀을 잘 들었어요?” and gives it the meaning “Did you listen (well/carefully) to what your teacher said?”. Insert ~시~ into the conjugated verb or adjective before the speech ending: 가시다, 읽으시다, and polite ~세요 forms.

cards.prompt: 그저께 회의 ___간 동안 무슨 말씀을 하셨어요?
cards.translation: What did you say during the meeting two days ago?
cards.explanation: The honorific ~시~ marks respect toward the person performing an action. HTSK also introduces special honorific vocabulary. In this sentence, “시” completes the blank in “그저께 회의 시간 동안 무슨 말씀을 하셨어요?” and gives it the meaning “What did you say during the meeting two days ago?”. Insert ~시~ into the conjugated verb or adjective before the speech ending: 가시다, 읽으시다, and polite ~세요 forms.

cards.translation: Before the meeting finishes, the vice principal will speak
cards.explanation: The honorific ~시~ marks respect toward the person performing an action. HTSK also introduces special honorific vocabulary. In this sentence, “말씀하실” completes the blank in “회의가 끝나기 전에 교감선생님이 말씀하실 거예요” and gives it the meaning “Before the meeting finishes, the vice principal will speak”. Insert ~시~ into the conjugated verb or adjective before the speech ending: 가시다, 읽으시다, and polite ~세요 forms.

cards.prompt: 부장님이 그 일을 망쳐서 부장님이 ___는 것을 듣는 사람이 별로 없어요
cards.translation: There aren’t really that many people who listen to the boss because he ruined that job
cards.explanation: The honorific ~시~ marks respect toward the person performing an action. HTSK also introduces special honorific vocabulary. In this sentence, “말씀하시” completes the blank in “부장님이 그 일을 망쳐서 부장님이 말씀하시는 것을 듣는 사람이 별로 없어요” and gives it the meaning “There aren’t really that many people who listen to the boss because he ruined that job”. Insert ~시~ into the conjugated verb or adjective before the speech ending: 가시다, 읽으시다, and polite ~세요 forms.

lessons.meaning: The honorific ~시~ marks respect toward the person performing an action. HTSK also introduces special honorific vocabulary.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it for teachers, elders, customers, senior colleagues and other respected subjects.
lessons.how_to_build: Insert ~시~ into the conjugated verb or adjective before the speech ending: 가시다, 읽으시다, and polite ~세요 forms.
examples: 어머님은 너에게 돈을 주셨어?
Did your mother give you money?
어머님은 미용실에 가셨습니까?
Did your mother go to the beauty salon?

lessons.title: Commands and prohibitions
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 40 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.translation: Don’t eat your food too fast!
cards.explanation: Korean imperative endings give commands and instructions with different levels of politeness and force. The lesson also covers negative commands. In this sentence, “먹지 마세요” completes the blank in “너무 빨리 먹지 마세요” and gives it the meaning “Don’t eat your food too fast!”. Attach the appropriate imperative ending such as ~아/어, ~(으)세요, ~아/어라 or ~(으)십시오. Use V-지 마 for a negative command.

cards.translation: Don’t be shy!
cards.explanation: Korean imperative endings give commands and instructions with different levels of politeness and force. The lesson also covers negative commands. In this sentence, “부끄러워하지 마세요” completes the blank in “부끄러워하지 마세요” and gives it the meaning “Don’t be shy!”. Attach the appropriate imperative ending such as ~아/어, ~(으)세요, ~아/어라 or ~(으)십시오. Use V-지 마 for a negative command.

cards.translation: Don’t do it like that!
cards.explanation: Korean imperative endings give commands and instructions with different levels of politeness and force. The lesson also covers negative commands. lessons.title: Saying when with ~ㄹ/을 때

cards.translation: I’m going to study in my house during vacation
cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을 때 means when or at the time that and can describe one occasion, a past time or repeated situations. In this sentence, “때” completes the blank in “저는 방학 때 집안에서 공부를 할 거예요” and gives it the meaning “I’m going to study in my house during vacation”. Attach ~ㄹ 때 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을 때 after another consonant. Use ~았/었을 때 for past context and N + 일 때 with nouns.

cards.translation: Where are you going to go during vacation?

Attach ~ㄹ 때 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을 때 after another consonant. Use ~았/었을 때 for past context and N + 일 때 with nouns.

In this sentence, “때” completes the blank in “선생님들은 회의 때 시간표에 대해 얘기했어요” and gives it the meaning “The teachers talked about the schedule during the meeting”. lessons.meaning: ~ㄹ/을 때 means when or at the time that and can describe one occasion, a past time or repeated situations.

lessons.title: Conditions with ~(으)면
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 43 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.prompt: 만약 지금 환경을 보존하지 ___ 미래에 더 큰 문제가 생길 것 같아요
cards.translation: If we don’t preserve the environment now, there will probably be bigger problems in the future
cards.explanation: ~(으)면 and ~ㄴ/는다면 express a condition such as if or when; ~ㄴ/는다면 can make the situation more hypothetical. In this sentence, “않으면” completes the blank in “만약 지금 환경을 보존하지 않으면 미래에 더 큰 문제가 생길 것 같아요” and gives it the meaning “If we don’t preserve the environment now, there will probably be bigger problems in the future”. Use ~면 after a vowel and ~으면 after a consonant. For verbs, use ~ㄴ다면 after a vowel or ㄹ and ~는다면 after another consonant.

cards.prompt: 그 연예인이 방에 ___ 양쪽에서 사람들이 그에게 다가가요

cards.explanation: ~(으)면 and ~ㄴ/는다면 express a condition such as if or when; ~ㄴ/는다면 can make the situation more hypothetical. Use ~면 after a vowel and ~으면 after a consonant. For verbs, use ~ㄴ다면 after a vowel or ㄹ and ~는다면 after another consonant.

In this sentence, “공부했으면” completes the blank in “내가 공부했으면 시험을 합격했을 것이다” and gives it the meaning “If I studied, I would have passed the test”. Use ~면 after a vowel and ~으면 after a consonant. For verbs, use ~ㄴ다면 after a vowel or ㄹ and ~는다면 after another consonant.

cards.translation: If I ate, I wouldn’t have been hungry
cards.explanation: ~(으)면 and ~ㄴ/는다면 express a condition such as if or when; ~ㄴ/는다면 can make the situation more hypothetical. In this sentence, “먹었으면” completes the blank in “내가 밥을 먹었으면 배고프지 않았을 것이다” and gives it the meaning “If I ate, I wouldn’t have been hungry”. Use ~면 after a vowel and ~으면 after a consonant. For verbs, use ~ㄴ다면 after a vowel or ㄹ and ~는다면 after another consonant.

cards.translation: If I met my friend, it would have been fun
cards.explanation: ~(으)면 and ~ㄴ/는다면 express a condition such as if or when; ~ㄴ/는다면 can make the situation more hypothetical. In this sentence, “만났으면” completes the blank in “친구를 만났으면 재미있었을 것이다” and gives it the meaning “If I met my friend, it would have been fun”. Use ~면 after a vowel and ~으면 after a consonant. For verbs, use ~ㄴ다면 after a vowel or ㄹ and ~는다면 after another consonant.

lessons.meaning: ~(으)면 and ~ㄴ/는다면 express a condition such as if or when; ~ㄴ/는다면 can make the situation more hypothetical.

lessons.how_to_build: Use ~면 after a vowel and ~으면 after a consonant. For verbs, use ~ㄴ다면 after a vowel or ㄹ and ~는다면 after another consonant.

lessons.title: Making suggestions
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 44 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.translation: Let’s go onto the stage together
cards.explanation: ~자, ~(으)ㅂ시다 and ~ㄹ래요 can make suggestions or ask about a shared intention. In this sentence, “올라가자” completes the blank in “무대에 같이 올라가자” and gives it the meaning “Let’s go onto the stage together”. Use verb stem + ~자 in casual speech, ~(으)ㅂ시다 in formal polite speech, and ~ㄹ/을래요 for a willingness or suggestion question.

Let’s talk about that with the teacher tomorrow”. Use verb stem + ~자 in casual speech, ~(으)ㅂ시다 in formal polite speech, and ~ㄹ/을래요 for a willingness or suggestion question.

In this sentence, “말자” completes the blank in “너무 안타까워서 내일 그 왕따를 놀리지 말자” and gives it the meaning “Let’s not tease that outcast tomorrow because it is too sad/sorry (of a situation)”. lessons.meaning: ~자, ~(으)ㅂ시다 and ~ㄹ래요 can make suggestions or ask about a shared intention.
lessons.when_to_use: Use them when proposing an action, choosing the ending according to politeness and the relationship between speakers.

lessons.title: Ability and possibility with ~(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다

Attach ~ㄹ 수 있다 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을 수 있다 after another consonant; replace 있다 with 없다 for the negative.

cards.translation: You can apply this lotion all over your body

lessons.source_title: Ability and possibility with ~(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다

cards.translation: We need to make a strong character
cards.explanation: ~아/어야 하다 expresses obligation, must or have to. ~ㄹ/을 필요가 있다 expresses the need to do something. In this sentence, “필요가” completes the blank in “강한 캐릭터를 만들 필요가 있어요” and gives it the meaning “We need to make a strong character”. Use the normal 아/어 form before 야 하다. Attach ~ㄹ 필요가 있다 after a vowel or ㄹ and ~을 필요가 있다 after another consonant.

lessons.meaning: ~아/어야 하다 expresses obligation, must or have to. ~ㄹ/을 필요가 있다 expresses the need to do something.
lessons.when_to_use: Use these forms for duties, requirements and necessary actions.
lessons.how_to_build: Use the normal 아/어 form before 야 하다. Attach ~ㄹ 필요가 있다 after a vowel or ㄹ and ~을 필요가 있다 after another consonant.
examples: 밥을 먹어야 하겠다
I will have to eat rice
우리 회사는 새로운 복사기가 필요해요
Our office needs a new photocopier
그 영화가 영웅 캐릭터가 필요해요
That movie needs a hero character

lessons.title: Contrast with ~지만
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 47 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.prompt: 머리를 창문 너머로 ___ 밖에 있는 친구가 저를 보지 않았어요
cards.translation: I stuck my head out of the window, but my friend outside didn’t see me
cards.explanation: ~지만 connects clauses with contrast: but or although. HTSK also compares it with related contrast expressions. In this sentence, “내밀었지만” completes the blank in “머리를 창문 너머로 내밀었지만 밖에 있는 친구가 저를 보지 않았어요” and gives it the meaning “I stuck my head out of the window, but my friend outside didn’t see me”. Attach ~지만 directly to a verb, adjective or noun predicate; mark past or future tense before it when needed.

cards.translation: I want to eat. But, I am not hungry.
cards.explanation: ~지만 connects clauses with contrast: but or although. HTSK also compares it with related contrast expressions. In this sentence, “하지만” completes the blank in “저는 먹고 싶어요. 하지만 배고프지 않아요” and gives it the meaning “I want to eat. But, I am not hungry.”. Attach ~지만 directly to a verb, adjective or noun predicate; mark past or future tense before it when needed.

cards.translation: I want to eat but I am not hungry.
cards.explanation: ~지만 connects clauses with contrast: but or although. HTSK also compares it with related contrast expressions. In this sentence, “싶지만” completes the blank in “저는 먹고 싶지만 배고프지 않아요” and gives it the meaning “I want to eat but I am not hungry.”. Attach ~지만 directly to a verb, adjective or noun predicate; mark past or future tense before it when needed.

cards.prompt: 그 아파트가 경비 아저씨가 ___ 안전하지 않아요
cards.translation: Even though that apartment (complex) has a security guard, it isn’t safe
cards.explanation: ~지만 connects clauses with contrast: but or although. HTSK also compares it with related contrast expressions. In this sentence, “있지만” completes the blank in “그 아파트가 경비 아저씨가 있지만 안전하지 않아요” and gives it the meaning “Even though that apartment (complex) has a security guard, it isn’t safe”. Attach ~지만 directly to a verb, adjective or noun predicate; mark past or future tense before it when needed.

cards.translation: I have to cut/mow the grass/lawn, but I don’t want to go outside
cards.explanation: ~지만 connects clauses with contrast: but or although. HTSK also compares it with related contrast expressions. In this sentence, “되지만” completes the blank in “잔디를 깎아야 되지만 밖에 나가기 싫어요” and gives it the meaning “I have to cut/mow the grass/lawn, but I don’t want to go outside”. Attach ~지만 directly to a verb, adjective or noun predicate; mark past or future tense before it when needed.

lessons.meaning: ~지만 connects clauses with contrast: but or although. HTSK also compares it with related contrast expressions.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when the second clause contrasts with, limits or unexpectedly differs from the first.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~지만 directly to a verb, adjective or noun predicate; mark past or future tense before it when needed.
examples: 부산에 가고 싶지만 차가 없어서 못 가요
Even though I want to go to Busan, I can’t go because I don’t have a car
물을 마셔야 되지만 물이 아직도 다 얼어 있어요
I need to drink water, but it is still all frozen
요즘에 한국어를 열심히 공부하고 있지만 아직도 잘 말할 수 없어요
Even though I am studying Korean hard these days, I still can’t speak well
그 연예인이 돈이 많지만 왜 그렇게 행복하지 않아 보여요?
That celebrity has a lot of money, but why doesn’t he look happy

lessons.title: Even if/even though with ~아/어도
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 48 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.prompt: 네가 건축가가 ___ 손으로 건물을 짓지 않을 거야
cards.translation: Regardless of if you become an architect, you won’t be building buildings with your hands
cards.explanation: ~아/어도 means even if or even though. 그래도 means even so, and 아무리 can add no matter how much. In this sentence, “되어도” completes the blank in “네가 건축가가 되어도 손으로 건물을 짓지 않을 거야” and gives it the meaning “Regardless of if you become an architect, you won’t be building buildings with your hands”. Attach ~아도 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어도 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해도. Add 아무리 before a concessive clause for emphasis.

cards.prompt: 어미를 ___ 이미 고양이 새끼가 다 죽었어요
cards.translation: Regardless of if you find the mother, the baby cats (kittens) all died
cards.explanation: ~아/어도 means even if or even though. 그래도 means even so, and 아무리 can add no matter how much. In this sentence, “찾아도” completes the blank in “어미를 찾아도 이미 고양이 새끼가 다 죽었어요” and gives it the meaning “Regardless of if you find the mother, the baby cats (kittens) all died”. Attach ~아도 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어도 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해도. Add 아무리 before a concessive clause for emphasis.

cards.prompt: 강가가 ___ 우리는 거기 내일 가야 돼요
cards.translation: Regardless of if the (area around) the river is far, we have to go there tomorrow
cards.explanation: ~아/어도 means even if or even though. 그래도 means even so, and 아무리 can add no matter how much. In this sentence, “멀어도” completes the blank in “강가가 멀어도 우리는 거기 내일 가야 돼요” and gives it the meaning “Regardless of if the (area around) the river is far, we have to go there tomorrow”. Attach ~아도 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어도 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해도. Add 아무리 before a concessive clause for emphasis.

cards.prompt: 그 남자가 ___ 그 문을 열 수 없을 거예요
cards.translation: Regardless of if that man is a magician, he is not going to be able to open that door
cards.explanation: ~아/어도 means even if or even though. 그래도 means even so, and 아무리 can add no matter how much. In this sentence, “마법사라도” completes the blank in “그 남자가 마법사라도 그 문을 열 수 없을 거예요” and gives it the meaning “Regardless of if that man is a magician, he is not going to be able to open that door”. Attach ~아도 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어도 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해도. Add 아무리 before a concessive clause for emphasis.

cards.prompt: 그 사람이 네 ___ 나는 그녀와 말을 안 할 거야
cards.translation: Regardless of if that person is your mother, I’m not going to talk to her
cards.explanation: ~아/어도 means even if or even though. 그래도 means even so, and 아무리 can add no matter how much. In this sentence, “엄마여도” completes the blank in “그 사람이 네 엄마여도 나는 그녀와 말을 안 할 거야” and gives it the meaning “Regardless of if that person is your mother, I’m not going to talk to her”. Attach ~아도 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어도 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해도. Add 아무리 before a concessive clause for emphasis.

lessons.meaning: ~아/어도 means even if or even though. 그래도 means even so, and 아무리 can add no matter how much.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when the result remains true despite a condition, difficulty or obstacle.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~아도 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어도 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해도. Add 아무리 before a concessive clause for emphasis.
examples: 밥이 있어도 저는 안 먹을 거예요
Regardless of whether there is food, I am not going to eat
태풍이 와도 내일 박람회에 가야 돼요
Regardless of whether there is a typhoon, I have to go to the trade show tomorrow
네가 어디 가도 나는 가고 싶지 않아
Regardless of where you go, I do not want to go
네가 나를 아무리 사랑해도 우리는 헤어져야 돼
Regardless of how much you love me, we need to break up

lessons.title: Permission with ~아/어도 되다
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 49 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.prompt: 저는 밥을 벌써 먹어서 다시 안 ___
cards.translation: I don’t need to eat because I already did
cards.explanation: ~아/어도 되다 asks or states whether something is allowed. ~지 않아도 되다 means do not have to. In this sentence, “먹어도 돼요” completes the blank in “저는 밥을 벌써 먹어서 다시 안 먹어도 돼요” and gives it the meaning “I don’t need to eat because I already did”. Attach ~아도 되다 or ~어도 되다 using the normal vowel rule. For do not have to, use V-지 않아도 되다.

cards.translation: You don’t need to put salt on this food
cards.explanation: ~아/어도 되다 asks or states whether something is allowed. ~지 않아도 되다 means do not have to. In this sentence, “넣어도 돼요” completes the blank in “이 음식에 소금을 안 넣어도 돼요” and gives it the meaning “You don’t need to put salt on this food”. Attach ~아도 되다 or ~어도 되다 using the normal vowel rule. For do not have to, use V-지 않아도 되다.

cards.translation: You don’t need to eat (rice) now?
cards.explanation: ~아/어도 되다 asks or states whether something is allowed. ~지 않아도 되다 means do not have to. In this sentence, “먹어도 돼요” completes the blank in “지금 밥을 안 먹어도 돼요?” and gives it the meaning “You don’t need to eat (rice) now?”. Attach ~아도 되다 or ~어도 되다 using the normal vowel rule. For do not have to, use V-지 않아도 되다.

cards.translation: You don’t need to shave your beard?
cards.explanation: ~아/어도 되다 asks or states whether something is allowed. ~지 않아도 되다 means do not have to. In this sentence, “깎아도 돼요” completes the blank in “수염을 안 깎아도 돼요?” and gives it the meaning “You don’t need to shave your beard?”. Attach ~아도 되다 or ~어도 되다 using the normal vowel rule. For do not have to, use V-지 않아도 되다.

cards.translation: You are allowed to be here
cards.explanation: ~아/어도 되다 asks or states whether something is allowed. ~지 않아도 되다 means do not have to. In this sentence, “있어도 돼요” completes the blank in “여기 있어도 돼요” and gives it the meaning “You are allowed to be here”. Attach ~아도 되다 or ~어도 되다 using the normal vowel rule. For do not have to, use V-지 않아도 되다.

lessons.meaning: ~아/어도 되다 asks or states whether something is allowed. ~지 않아도 되다 means do not have to.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it to ask permission, give permission or reassure someone that an action is unnecessary.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~아도 되다 or ~어도 되다 using the normal vowel rule. For do not have to, use V-지 않아도 되다.
examples: 그 시험을 합격하기 위해 공부를 안 해도 돼요
In order to pass that test, I don’t need to study
지금 문을 열어도 돼요
You may open the door now
지금 문을 열어도 좋아요
You may open the door now
지금 문을 열어도 괜찮아요

lessons.title: Plans and expectations with ~ㄹ/을 예정/계획/준비
lessons.explanation: A concise practice lesson based on the HTSK Lesson 50 topic. Read the original explanation for additional detail.

cards.translation: I am scheduled to do it
cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을 예정, 계획 and 준비 express a schedule or expectation, a plan, and preparation for an upcoming action. In this sentence, “예정이에요” completes the blank in “제가 할 예정이에요” and gives it the meaning “I am scheduled to do it”. Attach ~ㄹ/을 to 예정, 계획 or 준비 after the appropriate stem, then use 이다 or 하다 as shown in the lesson.

cards.translation: I am scheduled to eat
cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을 예정, 계획 and 준비 express a schedule or expectation, a plan, and preparation for an upcoming action. In this sentence, “예정이에요” completes the blank in “제가 먹을 예정이에요” and gives it the meaning “I am scheduled to eat”. Attach ~ㄹ/을 to 예정, 계획 or 준비 after the appropriate stem, then use 이다 or 하다 as shown in the lesson.

cards.translation: We are scheduled to meet at 10:00
cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을 예정, 계획 and 준비 express a schedule or expectation, a plan, and preparation for an upcoming action. Attach ~ㄹ/을 to 예정, 계획 or 준비 after the appropriate stem, then use 이다 or 하다 as shown in the lesson.

In this sentence, “예정이에요” completes the blank in “수업이 4시쯤에 시작될 예정이에요” and gives it the meaning “The class is scheduled to start at about 4:00pm”. Attach ~ㄹ/을 to 예정, 계획 or 준비 after the appropriate stem, then use 이다 or 하다 as shown in the lesson.

cards.translation: The students are scheduled to write 수능 next month
cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을 예정, 계획 and 준비 express a schedule or expectation, a plan, and preparation for an upcoming action. In this sentence, “예정이에요” completes the blank in “학생들이 수능을 다음 달에 볼 예정이에요” and gives it the meaning “The students are scheduled to write 수능 next month”. Attach ~ㄹ/을 to 예정, 계획 or 준비 after the appropriate stem, then use 이다 or 하다 as shown in the lesson.

lessons.meaning: ~ㄹ/을 예정, 계획 and 준비 express a schedule or expectation, a plan, and preparation for an upcoming action.
lessons.when_to_use: Use 예정 for an expected schedule, 계획 for an intention, and 준비 for being ready or preparing.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~ㄹ/을 to 예정, 계획 or 준비 after the appropriate stem, then use 이다 or 하다 as shown in the lesson.
examples: 일을 곧 그만둘 준비를 하세요

증상이 계속 나타나면 병원에 올 준비를 하세요
